sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (da:DataAsset)-[:BelongsTo]->(dd:DataDomain) GROUP BY dd.name RETURN dd.name AS domain_name, COUNT(DISTINCT da), AVG(da.schema_version)')

question: Retrieve the count of LineageEvents recorded by ProcessingJobs that apply TransformationRules implemented in 'Python' and transform DataAssets within the 'Customer' business domain.
sql: SELECT graph.lineage_event_count FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (pj:ProcessingJob)-[:Applies]->(tr:TransformationRule), (pj)-[:Transforms]->(da:DataAsset), (pj)-[:Records]->(le:LineageEvent) WHERE tr.implementation_language = ''Python'' AND da.business_domain = ''Customer'' RETURN count(le) AS lineage_event_count') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(lineage_event_count INT PATH '$[0]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (pj:ProcessingJob)-[:Applies]->(tr:TransformationRule), (pj)-[:Transforms]->(da:DataAsset), (pj)-[:Records]->(le:LineageEvent) WHERE tr.implementation_language = ''Python'' AND da.business_domain = ''Customer'' RETURN count(le) AS lineage_event_count')

question: Retrieve the names of DataConsumers and the names of the DataDomains they consume data from, ensuring that each consumer-domain pair is listed only once.
sql: SELECT graph.consumerName, graph.domainName FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (dc:DataConsumer)-[:Consumes]->(da:DataAsset)-[:BelongsTo]->(dd:DataDomain) RETURN DISTINCT dc.name AS consumerName, dd.name AS domainName') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(consumerName VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', domainName VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[1]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (dc:DataConsumer)-[:Consumes]->(da:DataAsset)-[:BelongsTo]->(dd:DataDomain) RETURN DISTINCT dc.name AS consumerName, dd.name AS domainName')

question: Find DataConsumers that consume DataAssets from at least two different DataSources with a security classification of 'Confidential'. Return the consumer names and the count of such DataSources.
sql: SELECT graph.consumer_name, graph.COUNTDISTINCT FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (dc:DataConsumer)-[:Consumes]->(da:DataAsset)<-[:Generates]-(ds:DataSource{security_classification:''Confidential''}) GROUP BY dc.name RETURN dc.name AS consumer_name, COUNT(DISTINCT ds)') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(consumer_name VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', COUNTDISTINCT INT PATH '$[1]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (dc:DataConsumer)-[:Consumes]->(da:DataAsset)<-[:Generates]-(ds:DataSource{security_classification:''Confidential''}) GROUP BY dc.name RETURN dc.name AS consumer_name, COUNT(DISTINCT ds)')

question: List the top 5 DataSources that generate the highest number of DataAssets with a sensitivity level of 'Confidential'. For each source, also provide the average quality score of the generated assets.
sql: SELECT graph.DataSourceName, graph.AssetCount, graph.AvgQualityScore FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (ds:DataSource)-[g:Generates]->(da:DataAsset) WHERE da.sensitivity_level = ''Confidential'' GROUP BY ds.name RETURN ds.name AS DataSourceName, COUNT(da) AS AssetCount, AVG(g.quality_score) AS AvgQualityScore ORDER BY AssetCount DESC LIMIT 5') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(DataSourceName VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', AssetCount INT PATH '$[1]', AvgQualityScore DOUBLE PATH '$[2]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (ds:DataSource)-[g:Generates]->(da:DataAsset) WHERE da.sensitivity_level = ''Confidential'' GROUP BY ds.name RETURN ds.name AS DataSourceName, COUNT(da) AS AssetCount, AVG(g.quality_score) AS AvgQualityScore ORDER BY AssetCount DESC LIMIT 5')

question: Retrieve ProcessingJobs that transform DataAssets which are also consumed by DataConsumers with 'critical_dependency' set to true. sql: SELECT graph.JobName, graph.AssetName, graph.AvgSuccessRate FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (pj:ProcessingJob)-[t:Transforms]->(da:DataAsset)<-[c:Consumes]-(dc:DataConsumer) WHERE c.critical_dependency = true GROUP BY pj.name, da.name RETURN pj.name AS JobName, da.name AS AssetName, AVG(t.success_rate) AS AvgSuccessRate') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(JobName VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', AssetName VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[1]', AvgSuccessRate DOUBLE PATH '$[2]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (pj:ProcessingJob)-[t:Transforms]->(da:DataAsset)<-[c:Consumes]-(dc:DataConsumer) WHERE c.critical_dependency = true GROUP BY pj.name, da.name RETURN pj.name AS JobName, da.name AS AssetName, AVG(t.success_rate) AS AvgSuccessRate')

question: Find DataAssets that have been both generated by a DataSource and consumed by a DataConsumer within the same business domain, returning the asset name, the business domain, and the names of the DataSource and DataConsumer involved.

question: Identify the top 5 DataDomains with the highest number of distinct DataAssets that have been transformed by ProcessingJobs with a success rate below 85%, along with the count of such assets.

sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (dd:DataDomain)<-[:BelongsTo]-(da:DataAsset)<-[:Transforms]-(pj:ProcessingJob) WHERE pj.success_rate < 0.85 GROUP BY dd.name RETURN dd.name AS DataDomainName, COUNT(DISTINCT da) AS TransformedAssetCount ORDER BY TransformedAssetCount DESC LIMIT 5')

question: Find the top 5 ProcessingJobs with the highest average success rate in transforming DataAssets, including the job name and its average success rate, but only for jobs that have executed at least 10 transformations.
sql: SELECT graph.ProcessingJobName, graph.success_rate FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (pj:ProcessingJob)-[t:Transforms]->(:DataAsset) GROUP BY pj.name RETURN pj.name AS ProcessingJobName, AVG(t.success_rate) ORDER BY AVG(t.success_rate) DESC LIMIT 5') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(ProcessingJobName VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', success_rate DOUBLE PATH '$[1]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (pj:ProcessingJob)-[t:Transforms]->(:DataAsset) GROUP BY pj.name RETURN pj.name AS ProcessingJobName, AVG(t.success_rate) ORDER BY AVG(t.success_rate) DESC LIMIT 5')

question: Retrieve the names of DataConsumers that access DataAssets through 'API' with a usage frequency of 'Hourly', excluding those consuming assets from the 'Marketing' domain. Also, provide their compliance requirements.
sql: SELECT graph.ConsumerName, graph.ComplianceRequirements FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (dc:DataConsumer)-[c:Consumes]->(da:DataAsset)-[:BelongsTo]->(dd:DataDomain) WHERE c.access_method = ''API'' AND c.usage_frequency = ''Hourly'' AND dd.name <> ''Marketing'' RETURN DISTINCT dc.name AS ConsumerName, dc.compliance_requirements AS ComplianceRequirements') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(ConsumerName VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', ComplianceRequirements VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[1]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (dc:DataConsumer)-[c:Consumes]->(da:DataAsset)-[:BelongsTo]->(dd:DataDomain) WHERE c.access_method = ''API'' AND c.usage_frequency = ''Hourly'' AND dd.name <> ''Marketing'' RETURN DISTINCT dc.name AS ConsumerName, dc.compliance_requirements AS ComplianceRequirements')

question: Identify the top 5 DataAssets with the highest average transformation success rates across all ProcessingJobs, including their names, business domains, and sensitivity levels.
sql: SELECT graph.asset_name, graph.business_domain, graph.sensitivity_level, graph.success_rate FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (pj:ProcessingJob)-[t:Transforms]->(da:DataAsset) GROUP BY da.name, da.business_domain, da.sensitivity_level RETURN da.name AS asset_name, da.business_domain AS business_domain, da.sensitivity_level AS sensitivity_level, AVG(t.success_rate) ORDER BY AVG(t.success_rate) DESC LIMIT 5') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(asset_name VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', business_domain VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[1]', sensitivity_level VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[2]', success_rate DOUBLE PATH '$[3]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (pj:ProcessingJob)-[t:Transforms]->(da:DataAsset) GROUP BY da.name, da.business_domain, da.sensitivity_level RETURN da.name AS asset_name, da.business_domain AS business_domain, da.sensitivity_level AS sensitivity_level, AVG(t.success_rate) ORDER BY AVG(t.success_rate) DESC LIMIT 5')

question: Find the average success rate of transformations for ProcessingJobs that belong to the 'Finance' DataDomain and run in a staging environment.

question: Find the most frequently used DataAssets by DataConsumers, returning the asset name and the count of consumers accessing it, ordered by the count in descending order.

question: Identify the top 3 DataDomains with the highest average quality score of data generation. Only consider DataAssets with a schema version greater than '1.0'. Return the domain name and the average quality score.
sql: SELECT graph.DomainName, graph.AvgQualityScore FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (ds:DataSource)-[g:Generates]->(da:DataAsset)-[:BelongsTo]->(dd:DataDomain) WHERE da.schema_version > 1.0 GROUP BY dd.name RETURN dd.name AS DomainName, AVG(g.quality_score) AS AvgQualityScore ORDER BY AvgQualityScore DESC LIMIT 3') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(DomainName VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', AvgQualityScore DOUBLE PATH '$[1]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (ds:DataSource)-[g:Generates]->(da:DataAsset)-[:BelongsTo]->(dd:DataDomain) WHERE da.schema_version > 1.0 GROUP BY dd.name RETURN dd.name AS DomainName, AVG(g.quality_score) AS AvgQualityScore ORDER BY AvgQualityScore DESC LIMIT 3')

question: For each SystemEnvironment, calculate the total number of LineageEvents recorded by ProcessingJobs running in that environment, grouped by the event status. Return the environment name, event status, and the count of events.
sql: SELECT graph.EnvironmentName, graph.EventStatus, graph.EventCount FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (se:SystemEnvironment)<-[:RunsIn]-(pj:ProcessingJob)-[:RECORDS]->(le:LineageEvent) GROUP BY se.name, le.status RETURN se.name AS EnvironmentName, le.status AS EventStatus, COUNT(le) AS EventCount ORDER BY EnvironmentName, EventStatus') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(EnvironmentName VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', EventStatus VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[1]', EventCount INT PATH '$[2]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (se:SystemEnvironment)<-[:RunsIn]-(pj:ProcessingJob)-[:RECORDS]->(le:LineageEvent) GROUP BY se.name, le.status RETURN se.name AS EnvironmentName, le.status AS EventStatus, COUNT(le) AS EventCount ORDER BY EnvironmentName, EventStatus')

sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (pj:ProcessingJob)-[t:Transforms]->(da:DataAsset)<-[c:Consumes]-(dc:DataConsumer) WHERE t.success_rate > 0.95 AND c.usage_frequency = ''Real-time'' RETURN da.name, da.format')

sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (dc:DataConsumer)-[c:Consumes]->(da:DataAsset) WHERE da.sensitivity_level = ''PII'' AND c.critical_dependency = true RETURN dc.name, da.name, c.access_method')

question: Retrieve the names of DataSources and their associated DataAssets where the generation frequency is 'Daily' and the quality score is above 0.85, along with the DataSource's owner team and the DataAsset's business domain.
sql: SELECT graph.name, graph.owner_team, graph.name_1, graph.business_domain FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (ds:DataSource)-[g:Generates]->(da:DataAsset) WHERE g.generation_frequency = ''Daily'' AND g.quality_score > 0.85 RETURN ds.name, ds.owner_team, da.name, da.business_domain') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(name VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', owner_team VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[1]', name_1 VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[2]', business_domain VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[3]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (ds:DataSource)-[g:Generates]->(da:DataAsset) WHERE g.generation_frequency = ''Daily'' AND g.quality_score > 0.85 RETURN ds.name, ds.owner_team, da.name, da.business_domain')

question: Find the number of DataAssets consumed by each DataConsumer in the 'Real-time' usage pattern, grouped by the compliance requirements of the consumers.
sql: SELECT graph.compliance_requirements, graph.name, graph.asset_count FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (dc:DataConsumer)-[c:Consumes]->(da:DataAsset) WHERE c.usage_frequency = ''Real-time'' GROUP BY dc.compliance_requirements, dc.name RETURN dc.compliance_requirements, dc.name, COUNT(da) AS asset_count') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(compliance_requirements VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', name VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[1]', asset_count INT PATH '$[2]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (dc:DataConsumer)-[c:Consumes]->(da:DataAsset) WHERE c.usage_frequency = ''Real-time'' GROUP BY dc.compliance_requirements, dc.name RETURN dc.compliance_requirements, dc.name, COUNT(da) AS asset_count')

question: Count the number of DataAssets per DataDomain that have a schema version greater than '1.0', and order the results by the count in descending order.
sql: SELECT graph.name, graph.asset_count FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (da:DataAsset)-[:BelongsTo]->(dd:DataDomain) WHERE da.schema_version > ''1.0'' GROUP BY dd.name RETURN dd.name, COUNT(da) AS asset_count ORDER BY asset_count DESC') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(name VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', asset_count INT PATH '$[1]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (da:DataAsset)-[:BelongsTo]->(dd:DataDomain) WHERE da.schema_version > ''1.0'' GROUP BY dd.name RETURN dd.name, COUNT(da) AS asset_count ORDER BY asset_count DESC')

question: Find the average execution time of transformations for DataAssets consumed by critical DataConsumers (criticality_rating = 'High') grouped by the owning department of the ProcessingJobs.
sql: SELECT graph.owning_department, graph.avg_execution_time FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (dc:DataConsumer)-[:Consumes]->(da:DataAsset)<-[:Transforms]-(pj:ProcessingJob) WHERE dc.criticality_rating = ''High'' GROUP BY pj.owning_department RETURN pj.owning_department, AVG(pj.execution_time) AS avg_execution_time') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(owning_department VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', avg_execution_time DOUBLE PATH '$[1]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (dc:DataConsumer)-[:Consumes]->(da:DataAsset)<-[:Transforms]-(pj:ProcessingJob) WHERE dc.criticality_rating = ''High'' GROUP BY pj.owning_department RETURN pj.owning_department, AVG(pj.execution_time) AS avg_execution_time')

question: Count the number of LineageEvents per DataDomain recorded from ProcessingJobs that transform DataAssets with a schema version greater than '1.0', showing domain names and counts.

question: For each DataDomain, find the total number of DataAssets it contains, the average sensitivity level of those assets (assuming sensitivity levels can be ordered from 'Low' to 'High'), and the domain name. Sort the results by average sensitivity in descending order.
sql: SELECT graph.name, graph.total_assets, graph.avg_sensitivity_level FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (dd:DataDomain)<-[:BelongsTo]-(da:DataAsset) GROUP BY dd.name RETURN dd.name, COUNT(da) AS total_assets, AVG(CASE da.sensitivity_level WHEN ''Low'' THEN 1 WHEN ''Medium'' THEN 2 WHEN ''High'' THEN 3 ELSE 0 END) AS avg_sensitivity_level ORDER BY avg_sensitivity_level DESC') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(name VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', total_assets INT PATH '$[1]', avg_sensitivity_level DOUBLE PATH '$[2]')) AS graph

question: Find the total number of LineageEvents recorded by ProcessingJobs belonging to the 'Marketing' domain and running in 'Europe' region environments.
sql: SELECT graph.total_lineage_events FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (pj:ProcessingJob)-[:RECORDS]->(le:LineageEvent), (pj)-[:BelongsTo]->(dd:DataDomain), (pj)-[:RunsIn]->(se:SystemEnvironment) WHERE dd.name = ''Marketing'' AND se.region = ''Europe'' RETURN COUNT(le) AS total_lineage_events') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(total_lineage_events INT PATH '$[0]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (pj:ProcessingJob)-[:RECORDS]->(le:LineageEvent), (pj)-[:BelongsTo]->(dd:DataDomain), (pj)-[:RunsIn]->(se:SystemEnvironment) WHERE dd.name = ''Marketing'' AND se.region = ''Europe'' RETURN COUNT(le) AS total_lineage_events')

question: Identify the top 5 DataAssets with the highest average transformation success rate across all ProcessingJobs, including their names and business domains.
sql: SELECT graph.name, graph.business_domain, graph.avg_success_rate FROM JSON_TABLE(CONVERT(frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (pj:ProcessingJob)-[t:Transforms]->(da:DataAsset) GROUP BY da.name, da.business_domain RETURN da.name, da.business_domain, AVG(t.success_rate) AS avg_success_rate ORDER BY avg_success_rate DESC LIMIT 5') USING utf8mb4), '$[*]' COLUMNS(name VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[0]', business_domain VARCHAR(255) PATH '$[1]', avg_success_rate DOUBLE PATH '$[2]')) AS graph
sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (pj:ProcessingJob)-[t:Transforms]->(da:DataAsset) GROUP BY da.name, da.business_domain RETURN da.name, da.business_domain, AVG(t.success_rate) AS avg_success_rate ORDER BY avg_success_rate DESC LIMIT 5')

question: Find the average success rate of transformations performed by ProcessingJobs grouped by their job type and owning department, excluding jobs without a defined SLA requirement.

question: Determine the most frequently used transformation logic across all successful transformations (success rate > 0.95) and identify the corresponding ProcessingJob names and departments.

sql_json: SELECT frogql_traverse('information_data_lineage', 'MATCH (pj:ProcessingJob)-[t:Transforms]->(:DataAsset) WHERE t.success_rate > 0.95 GROUP BY t.transformation_logic, pj.name, pj.owning_department RETURN t.transformation_logic AS logic, pj.name AS job_name, pj.owning_department AS department, COUNT(*) AS usage_count ORDER BY usage_count DESC LIMIT 10')
